subject: DeltaPlus private GPU topology, egress headroom and scaling plan
messages:
From: infrastructure@deltaplus.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private pool sizing input and egress constraints (DeltaPlus)

Hi Jonas / Laura / Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we move towards a scoped private deployment inside our AWS VPC, our infra team needs concrete throughput targets and suggested topology so procurement can size the contract. Quick context: production workload is a mix of chat & long-form generation. Attached is a compact workload-profile.csv with request distribution, median token lengths, and peak concurrency observed in our pilot.

Specific asks:
- Recommended sustainable throughput (requests/sec) and p95 latency targets for a 512-token generation profile.
- Suggested GPU instance class and node counts for an initial 3-node staging and 10-node production baseline.
- Egress/network headroom you expect us to reserve (Mbps per node) and whether we should enable private peering vs NAT gateway (we’re currently NAT).
- Any cache warmup steps you recommend prior to cutover and expected cold-start amortization.

We have internal constraints around egress costs and a 3-week procurement window, so anything concrete helps. Also looping in Sara (ops) and our procurement alias.

Attachments: workload-profile.csv

Thanks,
--
DeltaPlus Infrastructure
infra@deltaplus.ai
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: infrastructure@deltaplus.ai, sara.choi@deltaplus.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-04T13:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private pool sizing input and egress constraints (DeltaPlus)

Sara / infra team — thanks for the data. I pulled the CSV and ran a quick sensitivity pass with our sizing model (attached). High-level summary up front:

- Recommended baseline target (prod): 1,200 concurrent request slots (concurrent inference contexts) with p95 <= 200ms for 512-token interactive prompts (with batching and prefix cache). This maps to ~3,000 requests/sec when peak batching is active; for conservative planning treat sustained throughput as 1,500 reqs/sec.
- GPU class: H100-style instances give best headroom for mixed long/short generation; however A10/A30 class with 8-bit quantization is a cost-effective option if you can accept a 10–15% latency uplift. Recommended initial commitment: 8 x H100-equivalent for production (spread across 2 availability zones) or 20 x A30-class if you need a lower-cost starting point.
- Node counts: staging 3 nodes (1 per AZ), prod baseline 10 nodes (5 per AZ) with 2-node warm pool (idle but preloaded KV cache) per AZ for burst absorption. Our sizing model assumes 32GB per GPU KV-cache and a 65% cache hit-rate after warmup.
- Network/egress: reserve 400 Mbps per H100 node as a starting headroom number (this includes model weights + token egress under peak batching). For A30-class plan 200–250 Mbps per node. Given your NAT setup, we recommend setting up a dedicated VPC peering/private link for inference egress to minimize NAT bottlenecks and reduce per-request jitter. NAT gateway adds non-trivial jitter and costs at scale.
- Warmup and cold-start: expect first-hour cold-start amortization where cache hit-rate ramps from ~10% to target 65% depending on request locality. Plan a 30–60 minute ramp with controlled synthetic traffic (we can provide a warmup script) and a rolling warm-pool preloader that fetches common KV prefixes.

Operational notes / margin:
- Admission control: set hard admission at 1.2x your prod baseline to trigger graceful degradation (reject non-critical low-priority requests).
- Quantization fallback: keep a CPU or lower-precision fallback path for low-cost bulk batch jobs.
- Monitoring: p95 latency, cache-hit ratio, and egress utilization per node are the three leading indicators to watch.

I attached the priv-pool-sizing-model.xlsx (simple knobs: concurrency targets, batch window, avg tokens per request, cache hit assumptions). I’ll also upload a short runbook for warm-pool choreography if that helps.

Propose a quick alignment call Thursday to finalize AZ placement and procurement numbers — does 10:30am PT work?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Platform Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: sara.choi@deltaplus.ai

Date: 2026-07-05T10:22:00-07:00

Jonas — this is extremely helpful, thanks. A few clarifications from our side after a brief infra sync:

1) We can stand up VPC peering but will need security/networking sign-off — expect a 1-week lead.
2) Our preference is to start on A30-class hardware to control burn; procurement asked for concrete monthly committed GPU count and a cost envelope.
3) We observed a median tokens/request of ~420 in the pilot and tail at ~2,300 tokens for few percent of requests (long-form). We need to understand how long-form tails will affect admission controls and whether you suggest separate queues for long-form vs interactive.
4) Attached are the vendor security questions — SOC-related proofs and network architecture diagram (security-questions.pdf).

On call timing: Thursday at 10:30am PT works for our infra and procurement. Can you include a brief slide on how admission control treats long-form tails and an example fallback policy?

Thanks,
Sara Choi
Head of Infrastructure, DeltaPlus AI
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: sara.choi@deltaplus.ai, infrastructure@deltaplus.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, procurement@deltaplus.ai
Date: 2026-07-06T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private pool sizing input and egress constraints (DeltaPlus)

Sara / team — great, thanks for the quick answers and the security packet. Final alignment and next steps before the Thursday call:

1) Procurement ask: baseline commit recommendation for A30 path — 20 A30 GPUs reserved for month-one (this follows our conservative mapping from the attached model and gives you ~1.1x headroom). If you choose H100 the equivalent commit is 8 GPUs. I’ll put both numbers in the slide.
2) Long-form traffic: we recommend two logical queues — interactive (short) and long-form (background). Long-form should be admitted preferentially into bulk lanes with lower-cost precision or quantized variants; keep a small portion of the warm-pool (10%) reserved for long-form to avoid cold-starts. Admission policy example: if tail tokens > 1,000 and observed p95 > 500ms, route to background queue and optionally throttle sampling rate. I’ll include concrete thresholds and a sample SLAs slide.
3) Egress and network: we’ll include a NAT vs peering cost/jitter comparison on the slide; short answer is peering for production. For your procurement window, include a clause allowing us to burst to a managed warm-pool for the first 30 days while you validate traffic patterns.

Attachments: I uploaded the two-slide summary deck to the Drive link (see related_links). On the call I’ll walk through the model, the assumptions (batch sizes, cache hit ramp), and an operational checklist for week-0 warmup.

Action items before the call (owners):
- DeltaPlus: confirm preference A30 vs H100 and share network owner contact (Sara).
- Redwood: produce 2-slide decision brief + sample admission-control JSON + warmup script. (Owner: Jonas / Karthik)
- Procurement: review commit numbers and ring-fence budget.

See you Thursday 10:30am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite with the agenda.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Platform Solutions
Redwood Inference
